description: Define an Azure Functions–based HTTP and event-triggered API surface backed by Azure Cosmos DB for scalable document reads and writes. Emphasize serverless scaling, partitioned data access patterns, resilient poison-message paths for queue triggers, and secure access via managed identities and least-privilege RBAC.
constraints: Cosmos DB access must honor least-privilege RBAC scopes; partition keys documented per container.
Function host configuration must forbid anonymous access unless explicitly gated at the edge.
No plaintext storage of connection strings — use managed identity or Key Vault references.
requiredCapabilities: Azure Functions runtime for HTTP APIs and asynchronous queue/event processing
Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API baseline) as primary scalable document store
Azure Storage queues or Azure Service Bus for asynchronous command and integration patterns
Application Insights–style observability for cold start latency, failures, and dependency calls
assumptions: Traffic can burst; cost controls (consumption caps, alerting) must be articulated alongside scale-out behavior.
Clients tolerate at-least-once delivery semantics for async paths with idempotent handlers.
topologyHints: Cosmos-heavy read/write paths partitioned by tenant or aggregate root to contain hot partitions.
Separate HTTP façade functions from durable background processors driven from queues.
securityBaselineHints: Private endpoints or VNet integration for Cosmos DB where policy requires confined data-plane paths.
Key rotation and Defender recommendations tracked as operational backlog items.
